title: Finite-Fault Slip Model (Greece Slip Model Database)
description: Schema for a single published finite-fault slip model of an earthquake in Greece. One file = one model (a given earthquake may have several models, from different authors/methods, each as its own record). Field set follows the parameterization described in Bonatis & Vavlas (this review) and is aligned with the SRCMOD .fsp convention (Mai & Thingbaijam, 2014) for interoperability.

schema_version.description: Schema revision the record was written for. 1.1.0 = this revision (adds status, segment name, reference_point.position/along_strike_km/down_dip_km, provenance.data_origin/source_figure/verified_by/uncertainty_notes and further inversion.data_types); records written for 1.0.0 remain valid and keep 1.0.0.

status.description: Publication status of the record. Drafts (work in progress, e.g. still containing placeholders) are validated but never published to the site.

event.description: Properties of the earthquake itself (shared across all models of the same event).

event_id.description: Stable identifier shared by all models of this earthquake, e.g. arkalochori2021

tectonic_setting.description: e.g. 'Hellenic Subduction Zone', 'Aegean back-arc extension', 'Kephalonia Transform Fault Zone'

reference.description: Bibliographic source of this specific model.

inversion.description: How the model was derived (paper section 2.1).

data_types.description: Data used to constrain the slip model. teleseismic = teleseismic body/surface waveforms; strong_motion = near-field strong-motion (accelerometer) records; regional_waveforms = regional broadband seismic waveforms (including empirical-Green-function / source-time-function inversions of regional records); GNSS = GNSS displacements (static offsets or high-rate); InSAR = InSAR line-of-sight displacements; GPS_static = legacy alias of static GNSS offsets (prefer GNSS); field_mapping = field observations of surface rupture/offsets; tsunami = tsunami waveforms (tide gauges, offshore pressure sensors); coastal_uplift = coastal uplift/subsidence markers (e.g. raised shorelines); leveling = levelling (vertical geodetic) lines; macroseismic = macroseismic intensity observations; other = data not covered above (describe them in inversion.notes).

method.description: e.g. 'linear least squares with Laplacian smoothing', 'Bayesian', 'simulated annealing'

green_function_model.description: e.g. 'Okada uniform elastic half-space', 'layered 1D velocity model'

fault_segments.description: One or more planar fault segments making up the source geometry.

name.description: Optional human-readable segment label shown in the browser, e.g. 'North segment (subevent 1)'.

reference_point.description: Geographic anchor of the segment (e.g. top-center of the fault plane). Fault-plane frame (same as patches): along_strike_km is measured from the segment start in the strike direction; down_dip_km is measured from the top edge along the dipping plane. Strike/dip follow the Aki-Richards right-hand convention (the fault dips to the right when looking along strike), so the down-dip azimuth is strike + 90 degrees. Which point of the plane latitude/longitude refer to is given by position, or exactly by along_strike_km/down_dip_km when present; if neither is given, top_center is assumed.

position.description: Which point of the fault plane latitude/longitude refer to (its surface projection for points below the top edge). top_center = midpoint of the top edge; top_left = the patch-coordinate origin (along_strike_km = 0 on the top edge); center = centre of the plane; hypocenter = the event hypocenter (latitude/longitude are its epicenter; give its fault-plane position in along_strike_km/down_dip_km when known); unknown = not stated. If missing, the browser assumes top_center and labels it as assumed.

along_strike_km.description: Optional along-strike fault-plane coordinate of the reference point (same frame as patches). Together with down_dip_km it defines the placement exactly and overrides position.

down_dip_km.description: Optional down-dip fault-plane coordinate of the reference point, measured from the top edge (same frame as patches). Together with along_strike_km it defines the placement exactly and overrides position.

patch_grid.description: Discretization of the segment into along-strike x down-dip subfault patches (omit for uniform-slip models).

patches.description: Per-patch slip values. Omit or leave empty for uniform-slip models; use average_rake_deg + summary_metrics.max_slip_m instead.

along_strike_km.description: Position of patch center along strike, from segment start

down_dip_km.description: Position of patch center down-dip, from the top edge

rupture_time_s.description: Time of rupture onset at this patch, for kinematic (time-dependent) models

summary_metrics.description: Derived scalar values for cross-event comparison and scaling analyses (paper section 3.4).

model_variant.description: Optional flag for non-standard model types discussed in the paper.

source_file_url.description: Link to original author-supplied supplementary data, if available

data_origin.description: Where the slip values come from: author_supplied = numerical values supplied by the authors (e.g. supplementary file); srcmod = taken from the SRCMOD database; digitized_figure = digitized from a published figure; digitized_table = transcribed from a published table; derived = computed from other published values; other = anything else (explain in inversion.notes).

source_figure.description: Figure or table (and panel) of the source publication the values were digitized or transcribed from, e.g. 'Figure 5', 'Figure 3b', 'Table 2'.

verified_by.description: Who checked the digitized/transcribed values against the source publication.

uncertainty_notes.description: Free-text notes on the uncertainty of the stored values (digitization resolution, colour-scale quantization, etc.).
